change_log:
lifecycle_monitor_runner.py: _plan, _recorded, _cycle, _finish, _judge, _emit and _row folded away. run now plans each target (same select text, filters and order_by on the run's own connect) and drives each window's transaction itself. The judgement is the pure _verdicts: same sequence construction, persistence calls and first-candidate rule, and it also computes the reading ids. The emitted records come from the pure _records: same events, messages, field order and emission order. _unavailable is pure and returns its record plus the summary entry. _reading_id now takes the MonitoredSignal rather than a _Cycle; the key is unchanged. _append keeps its name and signature (cycle, window, readings, not_run) and builds the rows inline with the identical insert ... on_conflict_do_nothing. These keep their names and runtime lookups: _rules, _append, _evidence, _monitored, _engine, _flag_in, _rules_revision and _flag_reason. The flag still commits inside the last window's transaction, or a lone transaction when no window is due. A TransitionRefused from the bound writer is still an emitted refusal. Other exceptions still mark the signal unavailable before any emission. _Plan is removed; _Cycle and _Outcome remain.
lifecycle_store.py: _applied, _flag_id, _write, _refuse and _bound are inlined into their callers. _event_id is merged into the pure _event_row (same digest and row). transition keeps the same check order, refusal messages and now() call order: event_at first, then known_at per write. It also keeps the same queries: standing's events read, then a second events read only when the standing is flagged. Inserts are unchanged: the caller's connection when supplied, otherwise its own begin(). An IntegrityError in a caller's transaction still re-raises; one in its own transaction becomes a recorded refusal. Refusals are still written in their own transaction, and a duplicate one is suppressed. bind_writers builds the four writers with one nested factory; the writer parameter names are kept (signal, version, evidence, expected, reason; enroll's act).
cli/lifecycle_group.py: _window is inlined into lifecycle_readings. _compare is now pure and returns (lines, exit code); the command echoes the same lines and exits with the same code. Every patched global (_cited_baseline, _lifecycle_store, _pod_of, configured_pods, read_parameters) is still looked up at call time. Output texts are unchanged.
lifecycle_evidence.py: _lookback is inlined into LiveEvidence.for_window, still evaluated after _daily. Everything else is verbatim, including _consumed, _consumed_query and _observed_day.
lifecycle_projection.py: labeled_reason is folded into _flag, _latest_basis into _latest_and_not_run, and _state into signal_standing; the outputs are identical.
cppi/lifecycle_seams.py: the nested monitored, evidence and for_window closures are replaced by the pure module functions _monitored_signals and _window_evidence (the latter bound with functools.partial). readings_source is still called before read_evidence, per run.
wiring/lifecycle_root.py: the nested standing helper is inlined into a loop; the call order is the same.
Deliberately not preserved:
(a) On a concurrent-write refusal outside a caller's transaction, the raised TransitionRefused no longer carries the IntegrityError as a suppressed __context__. The type, message and __cause__ (None) are unchanged.
(b) In the seams, the ledger rows are now interpreted (admission_evidence) after store.admitted() is queried rather than before. This is observable only if a ledger row fails to parse.
(c) The seams import baseline_view at each monitored() call rather than at bind time, so a patch made after binding now takes effect.
Pure/shell: bind_lifecycle_monitor is declared pure because it only composes closures and performs no read, write or engine construction itself; its lambdas run the I/O when invoked by the runner.
